CHEN Shu⁃yun1 ， JIANG Hui1 ， LI Hai⁃yan1 ， HUANG Li⁃hua1 ， XU Jie1 ， YANG Hong2∗ （ 1. Department ofPharmacy，2. Department of Neurological Rehabilitation，Shanghai First Rehabilitation Hospital，Shanghai200090，China）ABSTRACT：OBJECTIVE To evaluate and analyze drug⁃drug interactions （DDI） in 360 rehabilitation patients in our hospital. METHODS A random sample of 360 patients （212 males and 148 females） with a mean age of $( 7 3 . 9 \pm 1 2 . 4 8 )$ years （16⁃93 years） was selected from our hospital′s January⁃December 2022 rehabilitation patients. Clinical pharmacists were analyzed by Lexi⁃Interact software to assess the incidence of drug interactions and the type of occurrence. RESULTS Lexi⁃Interact identified drug interactions in a total of 360 rehabilitation patients， 62 of these patients had drug interactions，of which 40 patients had class C drug interactions，18 patients had class D drug interactions，4 patients had class X drug interactions，and the mean number of medically prescribed medications $( 6 . 6 \pm 2 . 0 7 )$ . A total of 53 grade C drug interactions，18 grade D drug interactions，and 4 grade X drug interactions were screened. The most serious （ grade X） interactions were clopidogrel ＋ omeprazole，domperidone ＋ fluconazole，通讯作者杨红女学历硕士学位职称副主任医师研究方向为视神经脊髓炎谱系疾病的机理及治疗 and amiodarone ＋ moxifloxacin. CONCLUSION Most of our rehabilitation patients are patients with functional impairment，chronic diseases，elderly patients，and patients recovering from acute diseases，who need to take multiple drugs at the same time.
